title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/24/2026
Reason for Admission: Cough, fever, and shortness of breath.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 98.6F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fever, fatigue.
Respiratory: Positive for productive cough, shortness of breath.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea.
Neurological: Negative for confusion.

History of Present Illness:
[Copied Forward]: Patient is an 89-year-old female presenting with a three-day history of productive cough and low-grade fever. She reports dull chest pain on the right side. She denies any recent travel or exposure to known sick contacts.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for a lung abscess identified on a chest CT scan. Imaging confirmed the presence of a cavity with an air-fluid level, but no evidence of pneumonia was noted in other lobes. She was started on a prolonged course of intravenous antibiotics. She tolerated the treatment well and showed significant improvement in clinical stability and fever resolution. She is being discharged with a transition to oral medications.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Lung abscess

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875mg BID
Acetaminophen 650mg PRN for pain

Follow-up:
Follow up with primary care physician in 7 days for wound check and medication reconciliation.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
05/24/2026
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09

distractors.why: A lung abscess is documented, not pneumonia.
